elements.char: The rationale for having a single-coil reconstruction task (and for providing simulated single-coil
elements.label: text

elements.char: data), even though reconstruction from multi-coil data is expected to be more precise, is twofold:
elements.label: text

elements.char: (i) to lower the barrier of entry for researchers who may not be familiar with MRI data, since the
elements.label: text

elements.char: use of a single coil removes a layer of complexity, and (ii) to include a task that is relevant for the
elements.label: text

elements.char: single-coil MRI machines still in use throughout the world.
elements.label: text

elements.char: The DICOM images may be useful as additional data for training. Their distribution is different
elements.label: text

elements.char: from that of the ground-truth images, since they were acquired with a larger diversity of scanners,
elements.label: text

elements.char: manners of acquisition, reconstruction methods, and post-processing algorithms, so the application
elements.label: text

elements.char: of transfer-learning techniques may be necessary. Most DICOM images are the result of accelerated
elements.label: text

elements.char: parallel imaging acquisitions and corresponding reconstructions, with image quality that differs from
elements.label: text

elements.char: that of putative fully-sampled acquisitions and reconstructions. The ground-truth images may, in
elements.label: text

elements.char: many cases, represent a higher standard of image quality than the clinical gold standard, for which
elements.label: text

elements.char: full sampling is not routine or even practical.

elements.label: text

elements.char: Medicine Institutional Review Board.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Raw data was anonymized via conversion to the vendor-
elements.label: text

elements.char: neutral ISMRMRD format [18].
elements.label: text

elements.label: text

elements.label: text

elements.char: protected health information (PHI), manual checking of metadata in raw data files, as well as spot
elements.label: text

elements.char: checking of all metadata and image content.

elements.char: Knee k-space Data
elements.label: formula

elements.char: Multi-coil raw data was stored for 1,594 scans acquired for the purpose of diagnostic knee MRI.
elements.label: text

elements.char: For each scan, a single fully sampled MRI volume was acquired on one of three clinical 3T systems
elements.label: text

elements.char: (Siemens Magnetom Skyra, Prisma and Biograph mMR) or one clinical 1.5T system (Siemens
elements.label: text

elements.char: Magnetom Aera). Data acquisition used a 15 channel knee coil array and conventional Cartesian
elements.label: text

elements.char: 2D TSE protocol employed clinically at NYU School of Medicine. The dataset includes data from
elements.label: text

elements.char: two pulse sequences, yielding coronal proton-density weighting with (PDFS, 798 scans) and without
elements.label: text

elements.char: (PD, 796 scans) fat suppression (see Figure 3). Sequence parameters are, as per standard clinical
elements.label: text

elements.char: protocol, matched as closely as possible between the systems. The following sequence parameters
elements.label: text

elements.char: were used:
elements.label: text

elements.char: Echo train length 4, matrix size 320
elements.label: text

elements.char: 320, in-plane resolution 0
elements.label: text

elements.char: 5mm
elements.label: text

elements.char: 5mm, slice
elements.label: text

elements.char: thickness 3mm, no gap between slices. Timing varied between systems, with repetition time (TR)
elements.label: text

elements.char: ranging between 2200 and 3000 milliseconds, and echo time (TE) between 27 and 34 milliseconds.
